"For each item below, fetch its source and check that the recorded quote appears on the page and supports the item. A card item is a field of the plan in the producer's words, with the sources it cites: check each factual claim in it against those sources, and any value it carries against the page; what the plan will build, measure or predict needs no source, but a factual claim with no source is UNSUPPORTED. For a cost input, check that the page states the number for the setting given; whether it applies to this plan is not yours to judge. When the page states a different number for a num or rate item, give it as page_value. Decide only from the pages you fetch and the text below; do not read files. Return one status per item, under its ref: SUPPORTED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED or UNREACHABLE, with the page sentence you relied on.
Items, one per line:
p1:step: Org-Mol — SINOPEC Research Institute of Petroleum Processing / DP Technology / AI for Science Institute has this step in its pipeline: The hand-off from the Org-Mol machine-learning shortlist to synthesis: after screening over 6 million esters and filtering 461 monoesters on predicted dielectric constant, viscosity and thermal conductivity, they pick candidates for synthesis manually. This is exactly the slot where the card inserts Green-Kubo MD verification of viscosity and thermal conductivity before synthesis. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01720-4 | recorded quote: \"By further incorporating manual synthetic feasibility assessments based on experimental expertise, we select two candidates for synthesis, and their physical properties are experimentally measured.\"
p1:activity: The Org-Mol paper (the source of the 461-monoester shortlist) was published in npj Computational Materials on 11 July 2025; no later release from this collaboration was found. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01720-4 | recorded quote: \"Published: 11 July 2025\"
p1:c1: The shortlist-to-synthesis step is handled today with machine-learning property models only — the kinetic viscosity model then the thermal conductivity model — with no molecular-dynamics verification in between. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01720-4 | recorded quote: \"Monoesters with dielectric constants lower than 3.20 are then fed to the kinetic viscosity model and then the thermal conductivity model.\"
p1:c2: The working shortlist is 461 monoesters, of which only two are actually synthesized and measured; the rest are never independently verified. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01720-4 | recorded quote: \"Based on the aforementioned criteria of the kinematic viscosity and thermal conductivity, 461 monoesters are finally filtered out.\"
p1:c3: The team's stated reason for not running MD is cost at screening scale — a claim the card directly tests by parallelising Green-Kubo runs. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01720-4 | recorded quote: \"It can be seen that predicting these physical properties via MD is time-consuming for a single system and becomes unaffordable in a high-throughput screening scenario with thousands of candidates\"
p1:done: This team has not run the card's experiment: the 461 monoesters were ranked by ML models and only two were verified, experimentally by synthesis rather than by MD; no Green-Kubo viscosity/thermal conductivity verification of the shortlist was performed. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01720-4 | recorded quote: \"By further incorporating manual synthetic feasibility assessments based on experimental expertise, we select two candidates for synthesis, and their physical properties are experimentally measured.\"
p2:step: LG AI Research — GATE (Geometrically Aligned Transfer Encoder) has this step in its pipeline: The final validation stage (Fig. 2f) of their five-stage AI-enabled high-throughput screening workflow for single-phase immersion cooling fluids: after GATE screens billions of candidates down to a shortlist, the chosen few are validated before deployment. The card's MD verification of viscosity and thermal conductivity targets this validation step. | source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.23371v2 | recorded quote: \"Finally, experimental and literature validation confirm the physicochemical properties of selected candidates (Fig. 2 f), ensuring their suitability as single-phase immersion cooling fluids.\"
p2:activity: LG AI Research's GATE immersion-coolant paper was posted to arXiv on 27 October 2025 and last revised 31 October 2025 (v2), the most recent release found. | source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23371 | recorded quote: \"[Submitted on 27 Oct 2025 (v1), last revised 31 Oct 2025 (this version, v2)]\"
p2:c1: Validation today is experimental (TGA, DSC) plus literature values; transport properties like viscosity and thermal conductivity that their instruments cannot measure are taken from the literature rather than computed by MD. | source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.23371v2 | recorded quote: \"Decomposition temperature was measured using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA, onset point) and specific heat using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC, 20℃). For other properties that could not be measured with our available instrumentation, we surveyed the literature and incorporated reported values into Fig. 3 d.\"
p2:c2: The screening operates at billion-molecule scale but narrows to only four experimentally verified candidates, so most shortlisted molecules never get a physics-based check of their viscosity/thermal conductivity. | source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.23371v2 | recorded quote: \"Across the 41 million purchasable compounds and 2.54 billion in-silico reaction products examined, this screening yielded 356 candidates satisfying Criterion 1, and a total of 92,861 compounds meeting at least one of Criteria 1–6.\"
p2:c3: Four finalists are the extent of their verification stage; the pipeline is run by LG AI Research with Kyonggi University. | source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.23371v2 | recorded quote: \"From these, we selected four final candidates for experimental verification.\"
p2:done: LG AI Research has not run MD verification of viscosity/thermal conductivity on their shortlist; their validation stage is experimental measurement and literature survey only. | source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.23371v2 | recorded quote: \"Decomposition temperature was measured using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA, onset point) and specific heat using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC, 20℃). For other properties that could not be measured with our available instrumentation, we surveyed the literature and incorporated reported values into Fig. 3 d.\"
p3:step: Imperial College London Tribology Group (Dini) / Ewen (Bath) — MD-vs-ML thermophysical benchmarking has this step in its pipeline: Their head-to-head benchmark of machine-learning models against equilibrium molecular-dynamics (Green-Kubo) simulations for density, viscosity and thermal conductivity of organic liquids (lubricant- and cooling-fluid-sized molecules) — the exact property pair and force-field family the card deploys at shortlist scale. | source: https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/entities/publication/9423c271-1953-481c-8e8d-88eeb67e2535 | recorded quote: \"In this study, we benchmark ML models for the prediction of the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of lubricant-relevant organic liquids, and use MD simulations on a representative subset as an independent, physics-based assessment of the same properties.\"
p3:activity: The paper was published in Digital Discovery (RSC) with version of record dated 29 September 2026, a few weeks before this search. | source: https://pubs.rsc.org/dd/article/doi/10.1039/D6DD00260A/1362876/Benchmarking-Machine-Learning-and-Molecular | recorded quote: \"Received: 05 May 2026 Accepted: 18 September 2026 First published: 29 September 2026\"
p3:c1: Their MD practice today is Green-Kubo equilibrium MD on only eight molecules — two each from four chemical families including esters — at 40 and 100 °C, i.e. n=8 rather than the card's 100–1000. | source: https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/fa07c113-8958-4f1e-a010-0ef2bfc39e17/content | recorded quote: \"Finally, we apply Green–Kubo MD simulations to eight molecules, two from each of the four principal chemical families of the dataset, at 40 °C and 100 °C.\"
p3:c2: They use the same OPLS-family force field the card specifies, run in LAMMPS. | source: https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/fa07c113-8958-4f1e-a010-0ef2bfc39e17/content | recorded quote: \"All simulations were performed using the LOPLS-AA force field.\"
p3:c3: They already found chemistry-dependent force-field error for the property pair the card targets: viscosity is under-predicted for oxygen-containing (ester/ether) molecules, though the reference ranking is largely preserved. | source: https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/fa07c113-8958-4f1e-a010-0ef2bfc39e17/content | recorded quote: \"Viscosity errors are small for the pure hydrocarbons with LOPLS, but this property is consistently under-predicted for the oxygen-containing molecules; the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved.\"
p3:done: This group has already run a smaller version of the card's experiment — Green-Kubo EMD viscosity and thermal conductivity of organic liquids (including esters) benchmarked against ML — but on eight molecules, not a 100–1000 candidate shortlist and not the Org-Mol 461 esters; their finding that LOPLS-AA under-predicts ester viscosity bears directly on the card's OPLS-AA check-first tolerance. | source: https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/fa07c113-8958-4f1e-a010-0ef2bfc39e17/content | recorded quote: \"Finally, we apply Green–Kubo MD simulations to eight molecules, two from each of the four principal chemical families of the dataset, at 40 °C and 100 °C.\"

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
- Fetches content from a specified URL
- Takes a URL and optional format as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts to requested format (markdown by default)
- Returns the content in the specified format
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: if another tool is present that offers better web fetching capabilities, is more targeted to the task, or has fewer restrictions, prefer using that tool instead of this one.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - Format options: "markdown" (default), "text", or "html"
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in (text, markdown, or html). Defaults to markdown.

function.name: websearch
function.description:
- Search the web using the session's web search provider - performs real-time web searches and can scrape content from specific URLs
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Supports configurable result counts and returns the content from the most relevant websites
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

Usage notes:
  - Supports live crawling modes when available: 'fallback' (backup if cached unavailable) or 'preferred' (prioritize live crawling)
  - Search types when available: 'auto' (balanced), 'fast' (quick results), 'deep' (comprehensive search)
  - Configurable context length for optimal LLM integration
  - Domain filtering and advanced search options available

The current year is 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information or current events
- Example: If the current year is 2026 and the user asks for "latest AI news", search for "AI news 2026", NOT "AI news 2025"

numResults.description: Number of search results to return (default: 8)

livecrawl.description: Live crawl mode - 'fallback': use live crawling as backup if cached content unavailable, 'preferred': prioritize live crawling (default: 'fallback')

type.description: Search type - 'auto': balanced search (default), 'fast': quick results, 'deep': comprehensive search

contextMaxCharacters.description: Maximum characters for context string optimized for LLMs (default: 10000)
